**What we’re adding:** A “Sign in with Google” button that lets users log in with a Gmail address, while keeping all your safety rules in place. **Risk level:** **Amber** – we’re adding a login provider that gives the user access to their own data and your Supabase database. --- ### Safety parts we’ll build in | Feature | Safety part(s) that will be added | |---------|-----------------------------------| | Google OAuth login | • Uses **Supabase Auth** (no custom password logic)
• Users still see only their own rows (RLS enabled)
• The button is hidden until the user is logged in (no logged‑in data exposed)
• Secrets stay on the server (Google client ID in the Supabase secret store) | --- ### Quick one‑screen plan ``` What we are building: Google sign‑in for your Bolt site. Who uses it: Anyone with a Google account, who then gets a personal space. Risk level: Amber – risk because people log in. Day‑one features: 1. “Login with Google” button. 2. Successful sign‑in stores a user record in Supabase Auth. 3. User sees a friendly welcome message. Information it stores: user.email (public), user.id (private), etc. (private: logged‑in only) Logins: Google + email only, via Supabase Auth Money: none Built with: Bolt + Supabase Auth Steps: 1. In Supabase, enable Google in the Auth settings (client ID/secret). 2. Add a “Sign in with Google” button to your Bolt page that calls `supabase.auth.signIn(...)`. 3. Test by clicking the button and checking the console for errors. Safety: keys in Supabase secrets, RLS on all tables, single save point before each step. Does this look right? Yes→ proceed. No→ tell me what to change. ``` --- #### Step 1 – Enable Google in Supabase 1. Log in to your Supabase dashboard. 2. Go to **Authentication → Settings → External OAuth**. 3. Switch on **Google**. 4. Paste your **Google Client ID** and **Client Secret** (you’ll get these from Google Cloud Console). 5. Save. 6. Above the button, add a note: *“Tip: keep these secrets in Supabase’s secrets panel, not in your Bolt code.”* > **Checked:** Supabase will keep the secrets server‑side (not exposed to the browser). --- #### Step 2 – Add the sign‑in button to Bolt 1. Open the Bolt editor for the page you want to add the button to. 2. In the HTML section, insert: ```html ``` 3. In the **Script** section (or a new script block), paste: ```javascript const { createClient } = Supabase; // Bolt pre‑loads the Supabase SDK const supabaseUrl = ""; // from the Supabase settings const supabaseAnonKey = ""; // public key, safe to put here const supabase = createClient(supabaseUrl, supabaseAnonKey); document.getElementById('google-signin').addEventListener('click', async () => { const { data, error } = await supabase.auth.signIn({ provider: 'google', }); if (error) { console.error('Login error:', error); alert('Login failed. Check console.'); } else { console.log('Login successful', data); // You can redirect or show a welcome message here } }); ``` > **Safety note** – The only secret we’re using here is the `anon` key, which is meant for public use. The Google `client_id`/`client_secret` stay in Supabase secrets. 4. Save the page. 5. In the Bolt editor, click **Preview** and try the button. 6. **Proof** – If you see the console log “Login successful” and the alert shows your Google email, it’s working. --- #### Step 3 – Verify RLS and data privacy 1. In Supabase, go to **Database → Tables**. 2. Click on any table you will use. 3. Ensure **Row Level Security** is **ON** and the policy is “Allow logged‑in users to SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE on their own rows”. - If you don’t have a table yet, create a simple table `profiles` with columns `id`, `user_id`, `email`. - Add a policy like: ```sql create policy "Users can see own profile" on profiles for select using (auth.uid() = user_id); ``` 2. Test by creating two different Bolt accounts (different Google accounts). Verify you can’t see the other’s profile data through the Supabase dashboard or any API call. --- ### Final check & save point - Commit a **save point**: “Added Google sign‑in button”. - Run Bolt’s quick **ship check** (if available) or use: ``` python3 scripts/check_secrets.py --report ship-report.md ``` (If you’re in Bolt, you probably don’t have that tool; just be sure no keys are in the browser code.) --- **Next** 1. **Confirm the button works** (click and see the console). 2. If you want a “welcome” message after sign‑in, we can add a small script to read the user data from `supabase.auth.user()`. 3. Once you’re happy, we’ll push the changes live. Would you like to proceed with the steps above, or is there anything you’d like to tweak?
